emphasis flanking next to emoji and symbols: markdown-rs follows CommonMark 0.31, where Unicode punctuation includes the symbol categories; the micromark remark uses does not.

an ordered item that does not start at 1, after an indented code block: it cannot interrupt a paragraph, but after code there is none, so markdown-rs starts a list (CommonMark) and micromark reads a paragraph.
a CRLF right after a task marker: markdown-rs drops the line ending from the item text where remark keeps a leading one.
a block quote whose first line is indented code, opened right under a paragraph: micromark reads the code, markdown-rs keeps the paragraph going into the quote.

two seeded hostile documents with a ~~~ fence and an unclosed $$ fence or emphasis run that read differently; not minimised further, and not an autolink or an emoji difference (the difference stays with both removed).
